newsitem.title: USA: Applebee's sees no price war in its sector.
newsitem.headline: Applebee's sees no price war in its sector.

text.p: Applebee's International Inc, operators of one of the largest U.S. chains of sit-down eateries, has seen no evidence of the fast food sector pricing war spreading to its end of the business, said co-chief executive and chairman Abe Gustin.

"We haven't seen it in the casual dining segment ... As far as any price discounting, it hasn't happened in our industry and we certainly don't intend to get it started," Gustin told investors at a conference held here Tuesday by the Raymond James brokerage and investment bank.

Overland Park, Kansas-based Applebee's and its franchisees operate more than 800 Applebee's and Rio Bravo restaurants across the United States. The company expects to open 35 company-owned Applebee's and eight company-owned Rio Bravos this year, said chief financial officer George Shadid.
Applebee's is comfortable with the First Call consensus earnings estimate of $0.34 per share for the first quarter, up from $0.27 per share a year ago.

In 1996, Applebee's reported systemwide sales, including company-owned and franchisee units, of $1.54 billion, up 23 percent. Annual net earnings were $1.22 per share, up more than 30 percent versus 1995.

At the end of 1996, there were 148 company-owned restaurants and franchise units totalled 671. The company has two design prototype restaurants and is developing a third that will fit more customers in less space and run more efficiently, Gustin said.
U.S. fast food giant McDonald's Corp, based in Oak Brook, Ill., recently announced an aggressive price promotion to begin in April aimed at boosting sales.
